prompt:
The front desk has reported three date problems in the room-booking service: a booking that ends at midnight blocks the next day, the monthly report drops the 31st, and a stay over a clock change is one night short. Please correct the behavior without changing the JSON booking fields, the existing commands, or adding dependencies.

The public date helpers in `src/date-range.js` are `parseDate`, `formatDate`, `addDays`, `daysBetween`, `overlaps`, and `monthRange(year, month)`, with months numbered 1 through 12. Date-only values use local calendar dates. `daysBetween` must count calendar nights, `overlaps` must treat an end instant as free, and `monthRange` returns Date objects with an end at the first day after the month. In `src/bookings.js`, keep `hasConflict`, `addBooking`, `readBookings`, and `writeBookings` working for same-room bookings. `src/availability.js` exposes `isAvailable(bookings, start, end, room)` and `availableDays(bookings, start, end, room)`; the latter includes both requested calendar endpoints. `src/report.js` exposes `monthlySummary`, whose `{ month, totalNights, days }` JSON shape must remain intact and include every day. The CLI remains `node src/cli.js report --month YYYY-MM --file path` and prints that JSON. Keep the current Node 24 setup and existing behavior outside these date boundaries. Add a regression test for each of the three problems to the project's tests.

rubric.criterion: The final message states what was verified and identifies any verification that was not run (code cannot check this because it cannot assess the agent's report). Fail: claims all three problems (midnight end, missing 31st, clock-change night) are fixed when the change covers fewer, or claims tests were run that were not. Partial: reports `node --test` truthfully but does not say which of the three problems each new test covers, or does not mention that the clock-change case depends on the time zone it ran in. Pass: names each command run with its real result, ties one new regression test to each of the three problems, and says how the clock-change case was checked (for example with a pinned TZ).

The change fixes the cause at the place it lives, stays small, and leaves a regression test that would fail on the original code. Fail: patches the symptom (a special case at the caller), rewrites unrelated code, or adds no test that fails before the change. Partial: right place, but with extra churn (renames, reformatting, unrelated refactors) or a new test that would also pass on the original code. Pass: one change at the cause, nearby code left alone, and a new test that fails on the original code and passes now; the final message says which test that is. (code cannot check this because tests show the behaviour is right, not whether the diff is the smallest one at the cause)

authorship.note: single-family-authored (batch T1, owner decision 2026-11-20); second-family attempts failed or were not run, see DEBT D-122

verdicts.note: The prompt describes three problems and lists the public API and CLI, but does not tell the agent how to fix them (no specific algorithms, implementation patterns, or tool names).
The prompt specifies exclusive end semantics ('end instant as free', 'first day after the month'), calendar nights, and the exact CLI/JSON shape, so two competent readers should reach the same fix.
Fixture tests, comments, and docs do not mention exclusive ends, month-end boundaries, DST issues, or the specific bug patterns; they use ordinary dates that do not expose the edge cases.

Hidden tests cover exclusive ends, DST (spring clock change), leap day, month-end boundaries, and room separation, so a naive patch like special-casing January 31 or midnight would fail multiple checks.
The prompt fully specifies the expected behavior and constraints, the fixture compiles and runs, and hidden tests check stated requirements without contradicting the prompt or relying on timing.

items.note: Prompt asks to fix three specific date problems without prescribing methods or frameworks.
Fixture contains buggy date functions but no hints about midnight handling, 31st inclusion, or clock change fixes.
Hidden tests match three problems: midnight end freeing next day, monthRange including 31st, daysBetween across clock changes.
Developer can examine daysBetween, overlaps, and monthRange functions to fix described edge cases.
